To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a new method for learning to optimize combinatorial problems that is based on efficient active search and (2) we show that this new method outperforms all state-of-the-art approaches on combinatorial optimization tasks.

we propose three efficient variants of active search, show that they outperform state-of the-art machine learning based solvers on combinatorial optimization tasks, and demonstrate that they are effective at solving instances much larger than those used for training.

efficient active search can significantly improve the performance of machine learning based solvers for combinatorial problems and that these methods are able to effectively solve instances larger than those seen in training.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the efficiency of machine learning based methods that solve combinatorial optimization tasks.

the following three questions: (i) How can we make active search more efficient? (ii) How does active search compare to state-of-the-art learning based methods? (iii) Can active search solve instances that are larger than those seen at training?

the following questions: 1. How can we efficiently integrate machine learning based methods into a high-level combinatorial search? 2. How can we use active learning to improve the search performance? 3. How can we effectively use learned models to solve large instances?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed active search methods can be seen as a new paradigm for learning to search.
our work shows that efficient active search enables machine learning based methods to solve large instances of combinatorial problems.
our work provides a novel, efficient, and effective method for learning combinatorial optimization algorithms that is competitive with state-of-art methods on combinatorially hard problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
efficient active search is the most effective way to combine learned models with high-level search.
we propose and evaluate efficient active search methods that are able to solve instances of the vehicle routing problem that are much larger in size than those seen during model training.
we show that efficient active search is a very powerful and simple way of improving the performance of learned solvers for combinatorial problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
active search offers a very effective and simple approach to significantly improve the performance of machine learning based solvers.
active search is an efficient and effective way to improve the search performance and the scalability of a given learned model.
(efficient) adaptive search is a simple and powerful technique for improving the performance of learned models on combinatorial optimization tasks.
